title: Redundant column-completion reconfigure dispatched on every mount
description: The mount effect (line 343) already configures the column-completion compartment when the EditorView is created (lines 381-385), reading the same `availableColumns` prop. Because effects run in declaration order, the mount effect runs before the `[availableColumns]` effect (line 474). On mount, `viewRef.current` is already set, so the `[availableColumns]` effect immediately dispatches a `columnCompartment.reconfigure(...)` that produces a functionally identical compartment value (a fresh `autocompletion(...)` instance built from the very same prop). This is one extra no-op reconfigure transaction on every component mount. It could be avoided by gating the effect to skip the first run (e.g. an `didMount` ref) or by reconfiguring only when the column set actually differs from what the mount already installed.
evidence: Mount effect lines 381-385 build `columnCompartment.current.of(availableColumns?.length ? autocompletion({override:[columnCompletionSource(availableColumns)]}) : autocompletion())`. Effect at 474-483 then runs on mount (viewRef set) and dispatches `effects: columnCompartment.current.reconfigure(<identical expression>)`. Same `availableColumns` reference in the same render => identical intended config, yet a new extension instance forces CM to apply the reconfigure.
est_reduction: ~1 no-op transaction per mount; ~3 lines if a first-run guard is added
behavior_preservation: Behavior-preserving: the compartment ends in the same configured state; only the extra mount-time reconfigure transaction is eliminated.
